# W213: the neutral-C cokernel is generated by one row

W213 removes the irrelevant `A`, `B`, and `D` coordinates from W212's second obstruction.
Every element of `OneHandleBalancedCoreNeutralityCokernel` is represented by one ordinary
handle-relative `C` correction. The other three coordinate rows already lie in the original
constrained span and therefore vanish in this quotient.

The map `oneHandleBalancedCoreNeutralityClassHom` sends a relaxed `C` class to its class
modulo the constrained span. It is surjective, and
`oneHandleBalancedCoreNeutralityClassHom_eq_one_iff` identifies its kernel exactly: a
relaxed `C` class dies precisely when its bracket shift already belongs to the constrained
four-coordinate span.

For the current target, `neutralityObstruction_eq_one_iff_exists_relativeC_kernel` packages
the same statement as a single-row criterion. This remains a reduction, not a vanishing
theorem: the open work is now to determine which ordinary relative `C` classes become
character-neutral after allowing the constrained coordinate relations.

Every public declaration has exactly the standard axiom set `propext`, `Classical.choice`,
and `Quot.sound`.
